All my life I've tried to "empty the tank," so to speak, after all my runs. I think this is probably pretty common for races. But I'm not sure how common it is for training runs.

For example, I did a planned easy, long run today. But it was cooler than I thought, and I had a little more energy than I expected at the end of the run, so I ran the final .5 - .75 mi pretty hard. I'm wondering if this might be detrimental for a planned easy run since I wasn't holding my pace. I'll also do something similar for shorter runs.

Thoughts?
[Training] Do you finish your runs hard?

In the winter when running on an indoor track I break it up with sprints here and there or will try and do the last few laps pretty hard mostly to break up the monotony. I'm not sure if it is helpful or not but it keeps me going back when otherwise I may be tempted to quit.

When I am running outdoors the rest of the year I do feel the urge too give it my all near the end of a run just to see what I can do. The more I run the more impressed I am with my body and what it is capable of.

I find most interesting the desire to just run a bit for fun if I am out for a walk or hike much like when I was a kid and would just run for no reason at all other than I could.

Overall I believe if it feels good, feels right just do it. I think it is helpful but I have no scientific proof to back it up.
I always finish with a sprint unless it is a long run day, in which case I don't stop till the point where I couldn't sprint.
I always do my best to finish strong during a race. Because of this, I tend to push my training runs a little harder than normal at the end. Not an all out sprint but just an increase in pace.
